phn_hvi.preference_semantics: Hypernetwork input r is objective importance, as in existing PHN; cosine loss-ray is normalized 1/r to preserve rank_heavy meaning.

paper_reference_name: Improving Pareto Front Learning via Multi-Sample Hypernetworks

deviations: Same 5→64→128 zero-initialized FiLM hypernetwork as historical PHN-adapter, rather than generating all TiM4Rec parameters; full-network version is technically feasible but adds about 65x generator parameter overhead. See DESIGN.md.

HVI acts on minibatch-mean normalized task losses, matching the official Jura trainer aggregation (Multi_MNIST additionally provides per-example HVI). Frozen Adam/learning rate replaces Jura optimizer schedule.
Eight preferences and cosine coefficient 0.001 frozen from official Jura defaults; independent Dirichlet alpha=0.2 for five objectives. Existing six-point evaluation grid.

Independent inclusion-exclusion geometry matches official multifront normalized HV gradients, duplicate handling and adaptive reference. Use official negative cosine sign (paper equation 8 / code; printed equation 5 has conflicting sign).
Two-pass RNG replay reduces peak activation memory; same gradient as joint multi-sample backward. Preference input cloned to avoid mutable-buffer autograd aliasing.
No extra 30-epoch cosine-only Jura warmup; joint HVI+cosine begins at batch one inside the shared screening budget. This is an explicit method adaptation.

Existing preference vectors denote objective importance. The hypernetwork receives these same vectors; cosine alignment uses the normalized inverse-priority loss ray, as in EPO/FERERO loss-ray semantics. The official Jura trainer uses its sampled vector directly as a loss ray. This reparameterization and induced ray distribution are declared adaptations, frozen before data training.
